gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads tidy and open, its midline set high. Disorder is the opposite temperament, a raw display face whose lines look etched by laser at a constant width, with every glyph holding its distance from the next.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-thai: Disorder's lines never swell where a curve meets a stem, which gives it a raw, scratchy edge. And Noto Sans Thai answers with puffed, bead-like lowercase and rounds left open, so the two feel like opposites.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Noto Sans Thai Looped reads bold, since its lowercase bodies run so tall. Disorder is best at rod-stiff, uniform strokes with chaotic attitude, while the body font is best at spacious, open curve endings.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-vithkuq: Disorder's lowercase n keeps its arch and stem exactly matched, a rough display quirk you notice immediately. Noto Sans Vithkuqi sits beneath it with open throats on a, c, e and s, and barely any step from capitals to lowercase.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-warang-: Chaotic and raw, Disorder draws its marker-like line at a steady weight, with big lowercase set well apart. Noto Sans Warang Citi makes words read as solid blocks.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi has a deep midsection in the lowercase, and its rounds stay unsealed like an unlatched hook. Disorder, by contrast, is a raw display face with a simple one-tip stroke.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square brings a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Disorder, in turn, traces a single thick thread through each raw, widely spaced glyph, so the two sit as opposites.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-traditional-: Disorder traces one constant-width pen line through big, widely spaced lowercase, and the result feels raw and chaotic. It earns its keep large and short, while Noto Traditional Nushu fills the line.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-oxygen: Oxygen reads contemporary and clean, its curves never closing back on themselves and its lowercase nearly matching the capitals. And Disorder keeps its own curves thick right through the turns, so the headline feels raw above it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-preahvihear: Raw, scratchy and loud. Disorder outlines its letters in one steady thickness, and Preahvihear follows with a lofty x-height and open letter mouths like a pried oyster shell.
